2024_176_m052124bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held May 21, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:02 p.m. with approximately 400 members of the audience present. Beyond recognitions for retirees, Teacher Appreciation Week and Mental Health Awareness Month, the Board approved a seven-item consent agenda, three administrative appointments, an Algebra 1 curriculum adoption, and five purchases including $370,920.00 to CNC Foundations, Inc. for Smith Middle School ground stabilization and $493,845 to Apple Computers for freshman iPads. President Schmidt also read a bargaining update stating that the district and the TEA have held 15 sessions to date and have agreed to bring in a MERC mediator, with the first mediation session set for May 22.
2024_176_m052124bdmtg.page:
**Meeting and attendance**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, May 21, 2024, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Called to order by President Schmidt at 7:02 p.m.; adjourned 9:49 p.m. Approximately 400 members of the audience attended. Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson were present, along with Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Burden, Pagel, Yancy, Milanov, Recker, DiPonio, Zawislak, Brinks and West. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

**Recognitions**
Danielle Clippard, Career Facilitator at Troy College and Career High School, was named the 2024 Outstanding Support Person of the Year from among 19 nominations; she received a $250 check from the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence and was also named a 2024 Oakland County Support Person of the Year, an Oakland Schools Education Foundation award carrying a $500 cash prize for one recipient in each quadrant of the county. Retirees for 2023-2024 were honored, with Mr. Pagel reading each name and length of service. Troy High senior and Student Board Representative Jayla Turner was the Student Spotlight honoree, introduced by Thomas Butcher of the TSD Creative Guild.

**Resolutions**
National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 6-10, 2024 (Anne/Hauff), 7-0. Mental Health Awareness Month for May 2024, noting May 9, 2024 as National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day and May 5-11, 2024 as Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week (Wilson/Philippart), 7-0.

**Consent Agenda (Hauff/Haupt, 7-0)**
Items A through G: minutes of the April 2, 2024 Board Workshop; minutes of the April 16, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report - March 2024; approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2024/2025 school year budget; Food Service Contract; and IA budget approval for 2024/2025.

**Personnel (all 7-0)**
| Appointee | Position | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aurel Malutan | Finance Director, effective July 1, 2024 | Two-year probationary, without tenure |
| Benjamin Cronin | Assistant Principal, Athens High School, 2024-25 | Two-year, without tenure |
| Kristin Crowe | Principal, Wass Elementary School, 2024-25 | Two-year probationary, without tenure |

Elementary and secondary personnel recommendations for Victoria Auten, Sierra Dietz and Anna Greenblatt were approved (Alic/Anne), 7-0. Algebra 1 mathematics materials for the 2024-2025 school year were adopted (Philippart/Haupt), 7-0, following a review of information presented at the May 7 Board Workshop.

**Business items (all 7-0)**
| Item | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Smith MS ground/soil stabilization | CNC Foundations, Inc. | $370,920.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Two Electric Combi Ovens (Wass) | Gold Star Products | $32,542.00 | Food Service Fund |
| EPIC system, Leonard and Bemis | Inacomp TSG | $424,952 | General Fund and 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| iPads and cases for freshmen | Apple Computers | $493,845 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund |
| Athens and Troy High stadium scoreboards and audio | Daktronics, installed by Johnson Sign Company | $170,500 inclusive of a 10% contingency | 2023 Bond Fund |

**Bargaining update**
President Schmidt reported four bargaining sessions with the TEA since April 16 and 15 sessions in total, recent focus on the school calendar, and agreement by both parties to bring in a Michigan Employment Relations Commission mediator beginning Wednesday, May 22. The district will use a portion of its fund balance to settle the contract. Schmidt cited Ann Arbor's 141 layoffs and $21 million in cuts as an outcome Troy cannot replicate.

**Public communication and other business**
Numerous speakers addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication, most urging a fair and equitable teacher contract; Audra Melton, Stephanie Zendler and Alex Karpowitsch announced school board candidacies, and TEA president Jason Cichowicz also spoke. Student representatives Teagan Pruitt, Nurayda Albeez, Marlien William and Jayla Turner gave year-end reports. Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Board designated Matt Haupt as its representative and Vital Anne as alternate to the 2024 Oakland Schools ISD electoral body and directed support for candidates Carol Finkelstein and Marc Katz for two six-year terms ending June 30, 2030, at the June 3, 2024 election (Alic/Anne, 7-0). The June 4 Board Workshop was rescheduled to Thursday, June 6 at 6:00 p.m. (Haupt/Anne, 7-0); the next Board Meeting was announced for Thursday, June 20 at 7:00 p.m.
2024_176_m052124bdmtg.verbose:
**Meeting identification and attendance**
The Troy Board of Education met May 21, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart and Wilson were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Burden, Pagel, Yancy, Milanov, Recker, DiPonio, Zawislak, Brinks and West. Approximately 400 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:49 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typing notation GH/jh.

**Outstanding Support Staff Award**
The Board opened with the Outstanding Support Person of the Year recognition, a category covering bus drivers, secretaries, paraprofessionals, student support aides, custodial staff, food service, technology, childcare and security. Nineteen nominations were received. The 2024 honoree is Danielle Clippard, Career Facilitator at Troy College and Career High School, nominated by one of her students; the nomination noted that she does the workload of multiple people, helped create the first Careers course this year, and sets up mock job interviews for students in her class. Her name was engraved on the Support Person Plaque to be displayed at her building for the next year, and she was surprised with a check for $250 from the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence; a short video of the surprise visit was shared with the Board. A representative from Oakland Schools attended to announce that Clippard was also selected as a winner of the 2024 Oakland County Support Person of the Year. The Oakland Schools Education Foundation awards four school support persons, one from each quadrant of Oakland County, with a $500 cash prize each and a framed certificate of recognition; those items were presented at the meeting.

**Retirees**
The Board recognized employees who retired or announced their intention to retire at the end of the 2023-2024 school year. Mr. Pagel read each name with the year service began: Ed Berky (Maintenance, All Schools, since 1993), Donna Black (Food Service, Wass Elementary, 2011), Carolyn Brown (Teacher, Wattles Elementary, 2002), Patrick Dawood (Teacher, Athens, 1999), Susan Fortuna (Teacher, Troy High, 1980), Tim Fulcher (Director of Athletics, Continuing Education and Enrichment, Troy Learning Center, 2008), Shelia Gannon (Transition Coordinator, Services, 1989), Mary Goetz (Teacher, Bemis, 1989), Todd Hensley (Purchasing Supervisor, Rankin, 2013), Susan Hill (Para-Professional, Martell, 2001), Joaquina Kapuscinski (Para-Professional, Bemis, 2007), Camille Lamesch (Teacher, Martell, 1996), Jill Martens (Para-Professional, Troy High, 2002), Mark Martin (Teacher, Boulan Park, 1999), Melven Moffett (Teacher, Leonard, 2011), Joni Pallas (Para-Professional, Larson, 2011), Joan Porter (Teacher, Barnard, 1987), Karen Reese (Teacher, Costello, 1996), Matthew Reimann (Teacher, Troy High, 2005), Tonia Romancheck (Teacher, Hamilton, 2003), Cheryl Rowley (Teacher, Hamilton, 2003), Pamela Russ (Teacher, Bemis, 1995), Kitty Schmidt (Teacher, Baker, 1985), Beth Soggs (Technology Director, Services, 2017), Luba Sordyl (Teacher, Athens, 2003), Roseann Sparbeck (Secretary, Athens, 1999), Sandra Tallant (Food Service, Larson, 1997), Ellen Talsma (Secretary, Troy High, 1999), Julie Tomasko (Para-Professional, Larson, 1995), Raymond Torres (Teacher, Smith, 2002), Bill Turner (Career and Technical Education Supervisor, Troy Learning Center, 2005) and Lynn Yagley (Para-Professional, Leonard, 1996). Retirees received a gift of appreciation for their years of service.

**Teacher Appreciation Week and Student Spotlight**
Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Hauff, the Board adopted a resolution supporting National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 6-10, 2024, reciting that teachers inspire and open children's minds, promote democratic equality and critical thinking, and that Troy teachers set the bar for excellence. Yes: 7, No: 0. For the Student Spotlight recognizing the TSD Creative Guild, Thomas Butcher returned to introduce Jayla Turner, a Troy High School senior and the Student Board Representative for Troy High, who shared her accomplishments and received a certificate of recognition.

**Mental Health Awareness Month**
Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart, the Board adopted a resolution recognizing May 2024 as Mental Health Awareness Month, in coordination with Oakland Community Health Network and other Oakland County school boards. The resolution states that one in five of all Americans, including children, experience mental health issues that could lead to school difficulties, physical problems and even suicide, and that May 9, 2024 is National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day while May 5 through May 11, 2024 is Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Additions, deletions and agenda-item public communication**
None reported for either item.

**Consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board approved items A, B, C, D, E, F and G: minutes of the April 2, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the April 16, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - March 2024; approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2024/2025 school year budget; the Food Service Contract; and IA budget approval for the 2024/2025 school year. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Personnel**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic, the Board issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Aurel Malutan, who begins duties as Finance Director as of July 1, 2024. Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board issued a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Benjamin Cronin as Assistant Principal, Athens High School, commencing with the 2024-25 school year. Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic, the Board issued a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mrs. Kristin Crowe as Principal, Wass Elementary School, commencing with the 2024-25 school year. Yes: 7, No: 0. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board approved elementary and secondary personnel recommendations for Victoria Auten, Sierra Dietz and Anna Greenblatt. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Curriculum**
A brief presentation reviewed information given at the May 7 Board Workshop on the Algebra 1 math program. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt, the Algebra 1 mathematics materials were adopted for the 2024-2025 school year. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Business**
Smith MS ground stabilization improvements (Hauff/Alic): the bid for ground/soil stabilization and improvement work was awarded to CNC Foundations, Inc. in the amount of $370,920.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. Wass oven purchase (Haupt/Philippart): the bid for two Electric Combi Ovens was awarded to Gold Star Products in the amount of $32,542.00, approved as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. Epic Communication and Security Platform for Leonard and Bemis (Anne/Alic): purchase of the EPIC system was awarded to Inacomp TSG in the amount of $424,952, approved as an expenditure of the General Fund and the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. iPads for freshmen (Anne/Haupt): the district will purchase iPads and cases from Apple Computers in the amount of $493,845, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. Stadium scoreboards and audio systems (Philippart/Wilson): the district will purchase new scoreboards and audio systems for the Athens and Troy High School stadiums from Daktronics with installation by Johnson Sign Company in the amount of $170,500 inclusive of a 10% contingency, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Bond Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Board President comments - bargaining update**
President Schmidt read a statement on bargaining with the TEA. The district and TEA bargaining teams have had four bargaining sessions since April 16 and a total of 15 sessions to date, with recent meetings focused on the school calendar and significant progress reported. The administration seeks a competitive compensation package that is sustainable over time, and both parties agree Troy's pay schedule should be aligned and among the tops in Michigan. The statement attributed an elongated bargaining cycle statewide to several formerly prohibited topics such as evaluation and teacher placement. The Troy School District will utilize a portion of its fund balance to settle the contract. Both parties agreed to bring in a Michigan Employment Relations Commission (MERC) mediator; the district's two most recent contracts were also settled with the help of an independent mediator. The first mediation session was set for Wednesday, May 22, with additional sessions planned as needed. Schmidt stated the district cannot afford to replicate the financial situation in Ann Arbor, with 141 layoffs and $21 million in cuts, and called for more state funding for public education.

**Public communication (non-agenda items)**
Speakers were: Marianna Perakis, TSD parent, on the status of teacher contract negotiations and a fair and equitable settlement; Dr. Audra Melton, former TSD administrator and current parent, in support of TSD teachers, who announced her candidacy for the school board; Mrs. Stephanie Zendler, former TSD administrator and current parent, likewise announcing her candidacy; Mr. Alex Karpowitsch, Troy community member, on the state of negotiations and district climate, announcing his candidacy; Mr. Nik Didocha, TSD graduate; Ms. Karen Hunt, TSD parent, requesting a list of transition resources for special education students graduating out of the program because Project Search has only 8 spots open; Reagan Feld, a junior at Troy High School; Mrs. Emily Byrne, parent and teacher; Ms. Heather Kelly, teacher; Mrs. Pat Grandy, TSD preschool teacher, noting only 16 days left of school; Mrs. Angela Clemence, teacher; Mrs. Melissa Batts, teacher; Mr. Steve Dunneback, para-educator; Mr. Andrew Shipp, teacher; Mr. Rob Holder, teacher; Ms. Jennifer Bell, teacher; Mrs. Lara Cornish; and Mr. Jason Cichowicz, TEA president.

**Student representative reports**
Teagan Pruitt reported for Troy College and Career High School, Nurayda Albeez for International Academy-East, Marlien William, a senior, for Athens High School, and Jayla Turner for Troy High School, each covering year-end activities.

**Oakland Schools Board of Education election**
Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board adopted a resolution reciting Public Act 419 of 2004, which amended election procedures for Intermediate School Districts electing board members at a meeting of representatives from constituent district school boards, requires a constituent board to designate its representative and identify the supported candidate by resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days prior to the election, and requires consideration at not less than one public meeting; the Board previously considered the resolution at an open meeting under the Open Meetings Act on May 21, 2024. The Board designated Matt Haupt as its representative and Vital Anne as alternate to the 2024 electoral body for the Oakland Schools Intermediate School District Board of Education, supported candidates Carol Finkelstein and Marc Katz for the two positions, each for a term of six years ending June 30, 2030, and directed Haupt to vote for them at least on the first ballot at the June 3, 2024 election. Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Board comments, workshop date change and adjournment**
Board members shared appreciation of teachers and a desire to reach a contract agreement soon. Citing conflicts in board member calendars, it was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Anne that the June 4 Board of Education Workshop be rescheduled to Thursday, June 6 beginning at 6:00 p.m. Yes: 7, No: 0. Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for Thursday, June 6 at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next Board Meeting for Thursday, June 20 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building. The meeting adjourned at 9:49 p.m.
